blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents can improve decision-making with world-model foresight, provided that predicted states accurately reflect post-action interfaces. Existing state representations fail to jointly capture interface layout, UI semantics, and explicit locations. We introduce Typed Spatial Markdown (TSM), a Markdown-style textual state representation for desktop web interfaces. TSM serializes block-level and atomic-level UI elements according to their spatial relationships, jointly encoding their types, visual semantics, explicit locations, optional control states, and hierarchical membership. To train a screenshot-to-TSM renderer, we construct AtomBlock-WebUI, a dataset with precise annotations at both granularities. By injecting element-type labels into HTML and directly extracting bounding boxes after rendering, we avoid annotation errors caused by post-hoc inference from webpage structures. Building on TSM, we propose MKD2World, a desktop web world model trained in two stages for current-state description and action-conditioned next-state prediction. During inference, the web agent queries MKD2World as needed and performs a ``digest'' step, in which it interprets each predicted state and extracts task-relevant evidence for selecting the best action. Experiments show that MKD2World-9B achieves an EleF1 score of 26.50 on the out-of-domain test set, outperforming GPT-5.6-Sol(14.98) by 11.52 points. Across Online-Mind2Web tasks, MKD2World-9B improves the success rate of the Qwen3.5-35B web agent from 22.94% to 37.61%, achieving competitive performance among leading open-source GUI world models. Code is available at https://github.com/OmniAI-Lab-CUHKSZ/MKD2World.
blocks.zh: 图形化用户界面(GUI)代理能够用世界模式展望来改进决策,前提是预测状态准确地反映行动后界面. 现有的状态表示无法联合捕获界面布局,UI语义,以及明确位置. 我们引入了 Typed Space Markdown(TSM),这是桌面网络界面的 Markdown 风格的文本状态代表. TMM根据其空间关系对块级和原子级UI元素进行序列化,共同编码其类型,视觉语义,明确位置,可选控制状态,以及等级成员. 为了训练一个截图到TSM的渲染器,我们构建了AtomBlock-WebUI,这个数据集在两个颗粒上都有精确的注释. 通过向HTML中注入元素型标签,并在渲染后直接提取边框,我们避免了从网页结构推论后产生的注释错误. 在TMM的基础上,我们提出MKD2World,一个桌面网络世界模型,经过两个阶段的培训,用于当前状态描述和动作条件的下一状态预测. 在推论中,网络代理根据需要询问MKD2World,并进行一个“digest'步骤,其中它解释每个预测状态,并提取与任务相关的证据来选择最佳行动. 实验显示,MKD2World-9B在域外测试集上取得了26.50分的EleF1分,比GPT-5.6-Sol(14.98)的成绩高出11.52分. 横跨在线视野2 Web任务,MKD2World-9B提高了Quen3.5-35B网络代理的成功率,从22.94%提高到37.61%,在领先的开源GUI世界模式中实现了竞争业绩. 代码可见于https://github.com/OmniAI-Lab-CUHKSZ/MKD2World.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: With the development of vision-language models (VLMs), graphical user interface (GUI) agents have become capable of completing interactive tasks in real-world scenarios ( Cao et al., 2026a ; Hu et al., 2026 ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) . At each decision step, an agent generates an executable action based on the task objective, current interface, and historical information. However, without sufficient understanding of webpage dynamics—including the functions of user interface (UI) controls and the logic of interface transitions—it may generate ineffective actions that increase interaction costs or cause irreversible errors, such as accidentally deleting important data or leaking private information ( Shen et al., 2026b ; Liu et al., 2026 ) . Action-conditioned world models offer a promising way to anticipate future interface states before execution, helping agents assess whether candidate actions advance the task while reducing risky real interactions ( Mei et al., 2026 ; Gu et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 随着视觉语言模型(VLMs)的发展,图形用户界面(GUI)代理已经有能力完成现实世界情景中的交互任务(Cao等,2026a; 胡等, 2026; 周等, 2026). 在每个决定步骤中,一个代理生成基于任务目标,当前界面,以及历史信息的可执行动作. 然而,如果不充分了解网页动态——包括用户界面(UI)控件的功能和界面过渡的逻辑——它可能会产生增加交互成本或造成不可逆错误的无效行动,例如意外删除重要数据或泄露私人信息(沈等,2026b;刘等,2026). 有行动条件的世界模式提供了一种有希望的方法,可以预见到未来在执行前的界面状态,帮助代理人评估候选行动是否推进了这项任务,同时减少风险的实际互动(Mei等,2026;Gu等,2025)。

blocks.en: The usefulness of such foresight depends on what state a world model predicts . Figure 1 compares representative GUI state representations and highlights the desired trade-off: preserving a complete, structured interface state without incurring the cost of pixel-level reconstruction. We argue that, to distinguish the consequences of candidate actions, a predicted state should preserve a complete yet structured account of the post-action interface, including both the elements that change and the surrounding context needed to interpret those changes—their semantics, locations, control states, and structural relations. At the same time, it should avoid the cost and instability of reconstructing every visual detail of a webpage. Existing GUI world models represent states as free-form descriptions of interface changes, structured interface representations such as the Accessibility Tree (AXTree) and Document Object Model (DOM) ( Zuo et al., 2026 ) , HTML rendered into webpages ( Koh et al., 2026 ) , or images generated directly by image generation models ( Guan et al., 2026 ) . Free-form text concisely conveys major changes but loses layout structure and substantial information from the next interface. Common AXTree and DOM serializations preserve parts of the interface structure, yet often omit explicit element locations and have incomplete visual semantics ( Wu et al., 2023 ) . Other structured textual representations retain some layout and locations, but support limited element types and omit UI control states, complete visual semantics, or interface block structure ( Cao et al., 2026b ) . HTML-rendered images may omit actual images or deviate from the real layout, whereas pure image-generation approaches are costly and often distort fine-grained text ( Zheng et al., 2026 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) . Thus, these representations do not adequately balance preserving a complete, structured interface state with avoiding the burden of full visual reconstruction. This limits the completeness of the interface information available to a world model and, in turn, to downstream agent reasoning.
blocks.zh: 这种展望的效用取决于世界模型预测的情况。 图1比较了具有代表性的图形用户界面状态表述,并突出了期望的取舍:保持一个完整的,结构化的界面状态而无需承担像素级重建的成本. 我们主张,为了区分候选行动的后果,预测的状态应该保留一个完整而有条理地叙述行动后的界面,包括改变的要素和解释这些变化所需的周围环境——其语义、地点、控制状态和结构关系。 同时,它应避免重建网页每个视觉细节的费用和不稳定性。 现有的GUI世界模型代表状态是接口变化的自由形式描述,结构化的界面表示,如可访问性树(AXTree)和文档对象模型(DOM)(Zuo等,2026年),HTML被制成网页(Koh等,2026年),或者图像生成模型直接生成的图像(Guan等,2026年). Free-form文本简洁地传达出重大的变化,但从下个界面中失去了布局结构和实质性信息. 常见的AXTree和DOM序列化保存了界面结构的部分内容,但经常省略出显性元素位置并具有不完整的视觉语义(Wu等,2023.). 其他结构化的文字表述保留了部分布局和位置,但支持有限的元素类型并省略UI控制状态,完整的视觉语义,或接口块结构(Cao等,2026b. HTML-还原的图像可能会省略实际的图像或偏离真实的布局,而纯图像生成方法成本高昂并经常扭曲精细的文字(郑等,2026;罗等,2025. 因此,这些表述不能在保持完整、有条理的界面状态与避免全面视觉重建的负担之间取得适当的平衡。 这限制了可用世界模型的接口信息的完整性,进而限制了下游代理推理。

blocks.en: To address this bottleneck, we introduce Typed Spatial Markdown (TSM) , a structured and spatially grounded state representation for desktop Web interfaces. TSM organizes rendered Web UIs into block-level and atomic-level elements according to their spatial relationships. Each entry encodes its type, visual semantics, bounding box, optional control state, and hierarchical membership, jointly capturing what an element is, where it appears, what it conveys, and how it is organized. Markdown provides a readable hierarchical serialization of this structured state. By retaining the interface information needed to compare action-induced changes without reconstructing the full pixel-level interface, TSM provides a compact and directly comparable state space for action-conditioned world modeling and downstream agent reasoning.
blocks.zh: 为了解决这个瓶颈,我们引入了Typed Space Markdown(TSM),这是桌面Web接口的一种结构化和空间化的状态代表. TMM根据空间关系将制成的Web UI组织成块级和原子级元素. 每个条目编码其类型,视觉语义,边框,可选控制状态,以及分级成员,共同捕捉一个元素是什么,在它出现的地方,传达什么,如何组织. Markdown提供了这种结构化状态的可读分级序列化. 通过保留在不重建完整像素级界面的情况下比较动作所引发的变化所需的接口信息,TMM为动作条件世界模型和下游代理推理提供了紧凑而直接可比较的状态空间.

blocks.en: Learning this state space from screenshots requires reliable UI element types and locations. Existing desktop Web UI datasets often extract them from the DOM or AXTree through rule-based parsing ( Wu et al., 2023 ; Gurbuz et al., 2026 ) . However, HTML structures are highly heterogeneous across webpages: tags and class names are typically tied to page styling and interactions, while role attributes are often incomplete, making unified and reliable semantic annotations difficult to obtain ( Gou et al., 2025 ) . Post-hoc DOM parsing can therefore assign types to visually invisible elements or yield misaligned bounding boxes; visual models may likewise localize elements away from their actual positions ( Fu et al., 2026 ) . To reduce ambiguities introduced by such post-hoc semantic inference, we construct AtomBlock-WebUI . A VLM generates HTML with reference to real webpage layouts and explicitly injects predefined UI element types. After rendering, we directly extract the coordinates of the corresponding typed DOM nodes. This pipeline provides visually aligned type and location supervision for the dual-granularity UI detector in our TSM renderer.
blocks.zh: 从截图中学习这个状态空间需要可靠的UI元素类型和位置. 现有的桌面Web UI数据集经常通过基于规则的解析从DOM或AXTree中取出(Wu等,2023;Gurbuz等,2026). 然而,HTML的结构在网页上差异很大:标签和类名通常与页面的造型和相互作用相捆绑,而角色属性往往不完全,使得统一而可靠的语义说明难以得到(Gou等,2025.). 任务后c 因此,DOM解析可以将类型指定为可视的隐形元素,或产生错配的边框;可视模型同样可以将元素从实际位置本地化(Fu等,2026年)。 为了减少这种事后语义推论带来的模糊,我们构建了AtomBlock-WebUI. 一个VLM会参照真实的网页布局生成HTML,并明确注入预定义的UI元素类型. 在渲染后,我们直接取出相应打入的DOM节点的坐标. 该管道为我们的TMM渲染器中的双角UI探测器提供视同型和位置监督.

blocks.en: Building on TSM and AtomBlock-WebUI, we introduce MKD2World , an action-conditioned desktop Web world model that predicts future TSM states from screenshots and candidate actions. MKD2World first learns to reconstruct the current interface in the TSM state space, and then learns action-conditioned state transitions with transition-aware objectives that emphasize the elements changed by an action. At inference time, it simulates a next TSM state for each candidate action. We further train the GUI agent to understand TSM and design a digest-based inference strategy, through which the agent interprets predicted typed, spatial, and stateful changes to select the action that best advances the user objective. The main contributions of this work are as follows: • Typed Spatial Markdown (TSM). We propose TSM, a structured and spatially grounded Web UI state representation that encodes UI semantics, explicit spatial information, control states, and hierarchical structures, together with a screenshot-to-TSM renderer. • AtomBlock-WebUI Dataset. We construct a 9.7k-scale desktop Web UI annotation dataset using a pre-injected automated annotation pipeline, providing element types and bounding boxes for both block-level and atomic-level UI elements to train the dual-granularity UI detector in the screenshot-to-TSM renderer. • MKD2World: A TSM World Model for Web Agents. We propose MKD2World, an action-conditioned desktop Web world model that predicts future TSM states from screenshots and candidate actions. MKD2World uses a two-stage training scheme with transition-aware objectives, and supports uncertainty-triggered, digest-based action selection by TSM-aware Web agents. • Comprehensive Evaluation and Online Validation. We propose EleF1 to evaluate TSM prediction accuracy, and demonstrate strong out-of-domain prediction and consistent decision-making gains on Online-Mind2Web and VisualWebArena.
blocks.zh: 在TSM和AtomBlock-WebUI的基础上,我们引入了MKD2World ——一个动作有条件的桌面Web世界模型,通过截图和候选动作预测未来的TSM状态. MKD2World首先在TMM状态空间中学习重建当前界面,再学习动作条件状态过渡,其过渡意识目标强调被动作所改变的元素. 在推断时间,它模拟每个候选动作的下一个TSM状态. 我们进一步训练GUI代理来理解TMM,并设计一个基于文摘的推断策略,通过这个策略,代理解释预测的打字,空间,和状态的变化来选择最能推进用户目标的行动. 这项工作的主要贡献如下: • 已打入空间标记。 我们提出TSM,一个有条理和空间基础的Web UI状态代表,它编码UI语义,清晰的空间信息,控制状态和分级结构,以及一个截图到TSM渲染器. • AtomBlock-WebUI数据集。 我们建造一个9.7克大小的桌面 Web UI使用预注入自动注释管道的注释数据集,为区块级和原子级UI元件提供元素类型和边框,以在截图-TSM渲染器中训练双相角UI探测器. • MKD2 World:TSM网络代理世界模式。 我们提出MKD2World,一种具有行动条件的桌面Web世界模型,通过截图和候选动作预测未来的TMM状态. MKD2World使用具有过渡感知目标的两阶段培训计划,并支持TSM-感知Web代理商基于不确定性触发,摘要的行动选择. • 综合评价和网上验证。 我们提议EleF1来评价TSM的预测准确性,并在Online-Mind2Web和VisualWebArena上显示强大的域外预测和一致的决策收益.

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Web UI Understanding and Datasets
blocks.zh: 2.1 网络用户界面理解和数据集

blocks.en:
Existing datasets obtain UI annotations either from webpage structure metadata or directly from screenshots.
Structure-derived datasets—including WebUI ( Wu et al., 2023 ) , SeeClick ( Cheng et al., 2024 ) , and PixelWeb ( Yang et al., 2025 ) —scale efficiently by leveraging AXTree or DOM information, but their labels depend on heterogeneous HTML, DOM, or accessibility conventions and often require page-specific heuristics to obtain unified semantic types and visually aligned boundaries.
Screenshot-based methods such as OmniParser ( Lu et al., 2024 ) and ScreenAI ( Baechler et al., 2024 ) avoid dependence on webpage structure but can suffer from category ambiguity, coordinate offsets, or errors inherited from individual recognition components; high-quality manually annotated datasets ( Nayak et al., 2025 ; Dicu et al., 2025 ) are limited in scale.
AtomBlock-WebUI differs from both lines by injecting a predefined semantic taxonomy into webpage HTML before rendering and extracting bounding boxes from the corresponding rendered nodes, providing visually aligned, dual-granularity (block-level and atomic-level) supervision for screenshot-to-TSM rendering.

blocks.en: 2.2 GUI World Models and State Representations
blocks.zh: 2.2 图形界面 世界模式和国家代表机构

blocks.en:
GUI world models support either inference-time action selection ( Mei et al., 2026 ; Gu et al., 2025 ) or training-trajectory synthesis ( Xiao et al., 2026 ; Zuo et al., 2026 ) .
Across both settings, the choice of state representation fundamentally determines which interface information can be predicted, compared, and used for action selection (Figure 1 ).
Existing state spaces include: (1) free-form change descriptions ( Chae et al., 2025 ; Gu et al., 2025 ; Shen et al., 2026a ) , which are compact but lack explicit spatial layouts and hierarchical structure; (2) structured text or AXTree representations ( Cao et al., 2026b ; Zuo et al., 2026 ; Xiao et al., 2026 ) , which preserve partial structure but do not consistently expose element locations, visually grounded types, and control states in a unified form; (3) executable HTML code ( Zheng et al., 2026 ; Koh et al., 2026 ) , which can retain page structure but whose rendered outputs may deviate from the target layout or content; and (4) future images ( Guan et al., 2026 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) , which retain rich visual information but incur high generation cost and are unreliable for fine-grained text and small elements.
These representations typically trade off spatial and hierarchical fidelity against prediction cost and visual grounding.
TSM targets this gap by representing visible UI states as typed, spatially explicit, hierarchically organized elements with control states and visual semantics, remaining efficient for action-conditioned prediction and downstream candidate-action comparison.
AtomBlock-WebUI provides visually aligned supervision for rendering screenshots into this state space, while MKD2World models action-conditioned transitions within it for Web-agent reasoning. Detailed discussion refer to Appendix D .

A block-level element is written as b = ( τ b , p ) b=(\tau^{b},p) , and an atomic-level element as e = ( u , c , τ e , p ) e=(u,c,\tau^{e},p) .

The bounding box is defined as p = ( x , y , w , h ) p=(x,y,w,h) , representing the center coordinates, width, and height of a UI element, with values normalized to [ 0,999 ] [0,999] .

Finally, we use Playwright to drive Chromium and render full-page screenshots.
The annotation program directly retrieves the yolo-* DOM nodes to
obtain bounding boxes. Figure 3 compares AtomBlock-WebUI with existing Web UI datasets in annotation source,
viewport controllability, viewport element density, and category balance.

Given a webpage screenshot, the renderer converts it into TSM using a YOLO26 ( Jocher et al., 2026 ) UI detector trained on AtomBlock-WebUI, PP-OCRv6 ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , and Qwen3.5-0.8B.
It first uses the UI detector to identify element types and coordinates and PP-OCRv6 to recognize text, then binds the recognized text to the corresponding elements.
Some regions are cropped and passed to Qwen3.5-0.8B for visual semantics.
Finally, the renderer constructs a UI Element Tree with containment relationships and sorts the elements according to their spatial relationships to obtain the TSM representation. Details are in Appendix E.2 .

blocks.en:
At each decision step, the web agent first generates a candidate action set 𝒜 t = { ( a k , i k ) } k = 1 K \mathcal{A}_{t}=\{(a_{k},i_{k})\}_{k=1}^{K} , where a k a_{k} is a candidate action and i k i_{k} is its intent.
The web agent decides whether to invoke the world model based on its confidence.
For each candidate action, MKD2World takes the current screenshot I t I_{t} and the candidate action a k a_{k} as input and predicts the interface state S ^ k \hat{S}_{k} .
The web agent compresses each prediction into a structured digest d k = Digest ⁡ ( I t , a k , i k , S ^ k ) d_{k}=\operatorname{Digest}(I_{t},a_{k},i_{k},\hat{S}_{k}) , which includes a textual description of the main changes, their consistency with the action intent, their effectiveness in advancing the task, and evidence from S ^ k \hat{S}_{k} .
Finally, the web agent aggregates all digests d k d_{k} and selects the best action to execute. In addition, we conduct TSM-aware training for the web agent, training it to describe interface states in TSM and improve interaction ability with MKD2World.

blocks.en: 4.1 AtomBlock-WebUI Evaluation

blocks.en:
We compare AtomBlock-WebUI with four desktop Web UI annotation datasets: ScreenParse-v2, WebUI-CHI23, WebUI-COCO, and UI-Elements. We first deduplicate each dataset.
For ScreenParse-v2 and WebUI-CHI23, we randomly sample 1,000 viewport pages from their training sets.
WebUI-COCO and UI-Elements use all 618 and 508 pages.
AtomBlock-WebUI uses the same set of 1,000 full webpages and reports two evaluation settings: AtomBlock-Top evaluates only the top 16:9 viewport of each page, while AtomBlock-Full averages the evaluation results over all viewports of the same page. Each dataset uses its native viewport resolution and retains only desktop viewports, predominantly 1920 × 1080 1920\times 1080 .

We randomly sample 20 pages from each dataset and score them with humans to validate the GPT judge against human ratings. Raters score independently with the same prompt,
blinded to dataset identity and GPT scores (Appendix I ; Table 1 ).

blocks.en:
We extract interface transitions from WebChain and MolmoWeb-HumanTrajs.
After quality filtering, domain-based splitting, TSM rendering, and focus annotation,
we obtain a 100k Current-State reconstruction training set and a 31k Next-State prediction training set.
We reserve 500 validation transitions for model selection and result analysis,
and evaluate all models on in-domain (ID) and out-of-domain (OOD) test sets.
Each test set contains 1,000 transitions across five action categories:
click, text/key, scroll, navigation, and other, with 200 transitions per category.
We further maintain a balanced website distribution as much as possible (see Appendix G.1 ). For metrics, EleF1 measures the similarity between the predicted TSM and the ground-truth TSM.
We report EleF1 for five action categories and use Overall to denote the average value. Format Success measures the ratio of generated TSM outputs that can be successfully parsed.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the effectiveness of MKD2World in improving web agent performance on Online-Mind2Web ( Xue et al., 2025 ; Deng et al., 2023 ) and VisualWebArena ( Koh et al., 2024 ) .
Online-Mind2Web contains 300 real-time website tasks.
After removing unavailable tasks and tasks heavily affected by network instability, we select 109 relatively stable tasks as our test set, including 25 Easy, 48 Medium, and 36 Hard tasks (see Appendix H ).
The interaction trajectories are reviewed by GPT-5.6-Sol under a unified criterion to determine whether each task is successfully completed.
The judge receives the task instruction, the full trajectory of screenshots in temporal order, the action history, the agent’s final answer, and runtime error logs.
An early stop by the web agent does not count as success.
We set success = 1 \mathrm{success}=1 only when the screenshots and action records show that all task requirements are completed;
ambiguous, incomplete evidence, or termination at the 50 50 -step budget yields 0 0 .
Additionally, we use 233 tasks from VisualWebArena as a supplementary benchmark to further evaluate the generalization ability of MKD2World.
Success on VisualWebArena is determined by the benchmark’s official checkers rather than trajectory quality.
After the agent stops, the checkers inspect the final page and the last submitted answer and return a binary score under rules.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we presented TSM, a complete structured interface state, and constructed viewport-controllable AtomBlock-WebUI with balanced types and precise boxes.
We further introduced MKD2World and proposed digest and TSM-awareness to strengthen WebAgent–MKD2World collaboration.
Empirically, MKD2World outperforms GPT-5.6-Sol on prediction accuracy and boosts Qwen3.5-35B by + 14.67 % +14.67\% on Online-Mind2Web.
Despite the improvements, due to the complexity and frequent updates of web interfaces, MKD2World cannot achieve pixel-level aligned prediction. Our current setting targets static pages; it does not yet perform temporal understanding of audio, video, or animation, nor predict audiovisual changes over the next time interval.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们提出了TSM,一个完整的结构化界面状态,并构建了可控取的取景口AtomBlock-WebUI,配有平衡类型和精确的框.
我们进一步引入了MKD2World,并提出了文摘和TMM认识,以加强WebAgent-MKD2World的合作.
经验显示,MKD2World在预测精度上优于GPT-5.6-Sol,并在Online-Mind2Web上将Quen3.5-35B提升为+14.67%+14.67\%.
尽管有所改进,但由于网络界面的复杂性和频繁更新,MKD2World无法实现像素级对齐预测. 我们目前的设定目标是静态页面;它尚未对音频、视频或动画进行时间理解,也未预测下一时段的视听变化。

blocks.en: We perform fingerprint-based near-duplicate filtering on screenshots from Multimodal-Mind2Web. Each image is converted to grayscale, resized to 17 × 16 17\times 16 with Lanczos interpolation, and encoded as a 256-bit difference hash (dHash) by comparing adjacent pixels in each row. Screenshots whose hashes have Hamming distance d H ​ ( h i , h j ) = popcount ⁡ ( h i ⊕ h j ) ≤ 5 d_{H}(h_{i},h_{j})=\operatorname{popcount}(h_{i}\oplus h_{j})\leq 5 are connected in a graph; each connected component keeps one randomly selected image. Subsequently, we use the filtered screenshots as layout references and generate HTML with Qwen3.6-Plus. We require the model to cover 8 atomic and 6 block types, inject yolo-* category labels and vary color schemes for visual diversity. Each image node is an tag with a data-caption attribute. We next inject CC3M images into pages. For each node, we encode its data-caption with MiniLM-L6-v2 and retrieve the top-50 candidates via FAISS. We then re-rank by aspect-ratio mismatch with the target region and randomly pick one of the top-5. The chosen image is resized to the node and written back to the HTML. We render pages with Playwright-driven Chromium and collect bounding boxes from nodes tagged with yolo-* labels. We retain the original image-injected HTML, so each page can be re-rendered under different viewports while producing consistent annotations. AtomBlock-WebUI comprises 9,683 full-page screenshots and 1,321,234 type–bounding box annotations, split into 6,906, 1,388, and 1,389 pages for training, validation, and testing.

blocks.en: D.1 Web UI Understanding and Datasets
blocks.zh: D.1 网络用户界面理解和数据集

blocks.en: Web UI understanding requires identifying visible interface elements together with their semantic types and spatial extents. Existing datasets and methods obtain such annotations primarily from webpage structure metadata or from visual recognition.
blocks.zh: 网络UI的理解需要识别可见的界面元素及其语义类型和空间范围. 现有数据集和方法主要取自网页结构元数据或可视识别。

blocks.en:
1. Structure-derived annotations. WebUI ( Wu et al., 2023 ) constructs UI datasets through rule-based parsing of the AXTree, extracting UI elements and their corresponding bounding boxes.
SeeClick ( Cheng et al., 2024 ) and MultiUI ( Liu et al., 2024 ) similarly derive annotations from webpage structural metadata, but are commonly used for task-oriented grounding rather than dense full-page annotation of all visible UI elements.
WebCode2M ( Gui et al., 2025 ) collects real webpage screenshots and DOM-node information to annotate webpage structures, whereas PixelWeb ( Yang et al., 2025 ) obtains visible element boundaries through DOM information and pixel-level rendering, with its public release including substantial mobile-web data.
These approaches benefit from available webpage metadata, but their labels depend on heterogeneous HTML, DOM, or accessibility structures; obtaining a unified semantic taxonomy and visually aligned element boundaries therefore often requires page-specific heuristics. 2. Screenshot-based UI understanding. Visual methods instead infer UI elements directly from screenshots.
OmniParser ( Lu et al., 2024 ) detects interactive regions but covers a limited set of categories and can be sensitive to model parameters.
ScreenAI ( Baechler et al., 2024 ) combines OCR, UI detectors, and image captioning models to generate large-scale annotations, whose quality may inherit errors from individual recognition components.
ScreenParse ( Gurbuz et al., 2026 ) uses VLMs for UI-element category prediction and quality filtering.
UICVD ( Nayak et al., 2025 ) and GenGUI ( Dicu et al., 2025 ) rely on manual annotation and provide high-quality labels, but at limited scale.
While screenshot-based approaches avoid dependence on webpage structure, they may still suffer from category ambiguity and coordinate offsets. AtomBlock-WebUI differs from both lines of work by injecting a predefined semantic taxonomy into webpage HTML before rendering and extracting bounding boxes from the corresponding rendered nodes.
It thereby provides visually aligned, dual-granularity annotations over both block-level and atomic-level elements.
Rather than targeting only task-relevant grounding or generic UI detection, it is designed to supervise screenshot-to-structured-state rendering for TSM construction.

blocks.en: D.2 GUI World Models and State Representations
blocks.zh: D.2 GUI 世界模式和国家代表机构

blocks.en:
GUI world models follow two broad paradigms.
For inference-time decision enhancement, a world model predicts the next interface state conditioned on each candidate action, and a value model scores the predictions to select the best action ( Mei et al., 2026 ; Gu et al., 2025 ) .
For training data synthesis, agents interact with world models over multiple steps to produce interaction trajectories that are then used for agent training ( Xiao et al., 2026 ; Fang et al., 2025 ; Zuo et al., 2026 ) .
Across both settings, the choice of state representation fundamentally
determines which interface information can be predicted, compared, and used for action selection. Figure 1 summarizes the central trade-off among representative GUI state representations: preserving rich, structured interface information while avoiding the cost and instability of pixel-level reconstruction. 1. Free-form textual change descriptions. WMA ( Chae et al., 2025 ) , WebDreamer ( Gu et al., 2025 ) , and WAC ( Shen et al., 2026a ) describe post-action interface changes as free-form natural-language text.
This representation is compact and easy for language models to generate, but typically does not explicitly encode element-level spatial layouts, does not provide a structured, comparable state, and makes it difficult to evaluate prediction accuracy or directly compare candidate outcomes. 2. Structured textual and accessibility representations. MobileDreamer ( Cao et al., 2026b ) uses structured text to describe mobile Web interfaces, capturing some hierarchical layout but supporting only a limited set of element types and omitting many interactive elements and block-level structures.
Qwen-AgentWorld ( Zuo et al., 2026 ) and WebWorld ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) predict AXTree representations in Web environments, and more broadly, AXTree and DOM have been widely adopted as structured observations for GUI agents.
However, these representations do not consistently expose explicit element locations or visually grounded semantics in a form suitable for state comparison, hindering direct use for pixel-aligned state prediction and candidate-action evaluation. 3. Code and image state representations. Code2World ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) and gWorld ( Koh et al., 2026 ) predict future states as HTML code that is subsequently rendered into images; however, the rendered pages often lack realistic visual assets and can diverge from real webpage layouts.
CUWM ( Guan et al., 2026 ) predicts future states directly as interface images, but incurs high generation cost and tends to produce distorted or blurry small text.
ViMo ( Luo et al., 2025 ) masks text regions, predicts a text-free image, and uses an LLM to infill text, but this decoupled generation lacks tight semantic grounding in spatial elements and can produce inaccurate fine-grained content.

在这两种情况下,国家代表性的选择都从根本上

Quen-AgentWorld(Zuo等,2026年)和WebWorld(Xiao等,2026年)预测了AXTree在Web环境中的表示,更广义地说,AXTree和DOM被广泛接受为GUI代理的结构化观测.
然而,这些表述并不始终以适合状态比较的形式暴露出明确的元素位置或视基语义,妨碍了直接用于像素相通状态预测和候选人行动评价. 3. 代码和图像状态说明。 Code2World(Zheng等,2026年)和gWorld(Koh等,2026年)预测未来状态为HTML代码,后被渲染成图像;然而被渲染的网页往往缺乏现实的可视资产并可能与真实的网页布局相去甚远.
CUWM (Guan et al., 2026) 将未来状态直接预测为界面图像,但需要高昂的生成成本并往往产生被扭曲或模糊的小文本.
ViMo (Luo等,2025年) 遮盖了文本区域,预测了无文本图像,并使用LLM来填充文本,但这种脱钩的生成在空间元素上缺乏紧凑的语义地平面,可以产生不准确的精细内容.

blocks.en: Prior work has studied UI understanding datasets, GUI element grounding, and action-conditioned world modeling, but these lines have not jointly provided a state space that is spatially explicit, hierarchically structured, and efficient to predict. TSM fills this gap by serializing complete UI states into typed spatial elements. AtomBlock-WebUI supplies aligned supervision for rendering screenshots into this state space, and MKD2World models action-conditioned transitions within it.
blocks.zh: 先前的工作研究了UI对数据集的理解,GUI元素地基定位,以及行动条件世界模型化,但这些线条并没有共同提供空间清晰,分级结构,高效预测的状态空间. TMM通过将完整的UI状态序列化为打入的空间元素来填补这一空白. AtomBlock-WebUI为将截图渲染到这个状态空间提供对齐的监管,MKD2World模型在其内部进行有动作条件的转换.

blocks.en:
The screenshot renderer converts a webpage screenshot into a TSM state using a YOLO26 detector trained on AtomBlock-WebUI, PP-OCRv6, and Qwen3.5-0.8B. A child block is contained in a parent if its center lies inside the parent and the parent covers more than 85% of its area. The block priorities are 0 for Navigation , Sidebar , and Footer , 1 for Form and Table , and 2 for Section (lower is high priority). So generic Section do not override function-specific blocks. For each atomic element, we first take blocks that contain its center; otherwise those covering at least 50% of its area. Among candidates, we keep the smallest block with the highest priority; unmatched elements stay at the TSM top level.
Qwen3.5-0.8B describes images and icons, and judges states of checkboxes, radios, and selects. For checkboxes and radios, we enlarge the crop to capture the same line. For selects, we extend the crop downward and treat the dropdown as open if options appear.

blocks.en:
Focus annotations exist only for changed transitions. Given states S t S_{t} and S t + 1 S_{t+1} , we mark add and update elements in S t + 1 S_{t+1} and record their spans to compute the Base–Focus Element Loss.
Directly comparing S t S_{t} and S t + 1 S_{t+1} may confuse rendering noise or minor positional shifts with actual changes. We therefore match elements between the two TSM states. For each element, we parse content, type, state, and bbox, and record its span in the TSM string.
For text-input actions, we first match the element at the action location. If multiple nearby elements share a similar shift, we keep them matched. We then match elements with aligned semantics and bboxes, then those with aligned semantics but shifted bboxes. Unmatched elements are labeled add only if they pass a reliability filter. A matched element is update if any of content, state, or bbox changes reliably.

直接比较St S_{t}和St + 1 S_{t+1}可能会将渲染出噪声或微小位置变化与实际变化相混淆. 因此,我们匹配两个TSM州之间的要素。 对于每个元素,我们解析内容,类型,状态,和bbox,并在TMM字符串中记录其长度.
对于文本输入动作,我们首先在动作位置匹配元素. 如果附近的多个元素有相似的转变,我们保持它们的匹配. 然后我们把元素配对成语义和bbox, 然后是那些配对的语义,但转换出bbox。 未匹配的元素只有在通过可靠性过滤器时才会被加标签. 匹配的元素是如果内容、状态或bbox有可靠变化时更新。

Each ‘ candidate_digests [ i ]‘ summarizes the World Model forecast for ‘ candidate_actions [ i ]‘. ## Input - ‘ goal_text ‘: final user task . - ‘ current_url ‘: current browser URL . - ‘ current_subgoal_trace ‘: actions already attempted . - ‘ supported_unified_actions ‘: allowed action types . - The attached image is the current viewport screenshot . - ‘ candidate_actions ‘: candidate actions in their original order . - ‘ candidate_actions_intent ‘: intended visible effect of each candidate action . - ‘ candidate_digests ‘: Digest outputs in candidate order . ## Selection rules 1. Align actions , intents , and digests by index . 2. Use the screenshot and action history as current evidence and each digest as forecast evidence . 3. Evaluate ‘ intent_alignment ‘ and ‘ task_progress ‘ independently . 4. Rank candidates by likely useful task progress , grounded by ‘ predicted_change ‘, ‘ intent_alignment ‘ and ‘ task_progress ‘. 5. Resolve an ‘ unclear ‘ digest using the current state , action history , and candidate intent . 6. Prefer candidates that break repeated ineffective attempts recorded in the action history . 7. Select exactly one existing candidate and copy its action and intent by index . ## Output Return a valid JSON object in this format : { " best_action ": { " candidate_index ": 0, " unified_action ": { " type ": " left_click ", " coordinate ": [500, 500] }, " action_intent ": " Expected visible change " } } - ‘ candidate_index ‘ is a zero - based integer in ‘[0, number_of_candidates - 1]‘. - ‘ unified_action ‘ equals ‘ candidate_actions [ candidate_index ]‘. - ‘ action_intent ‘ equals ‘ candidate_actions_intent [ candidate_index ]‘.

Rules : - Markdown must be the complete visible UI state after the action . - Markdown must start with ‘[ Environment : Web ]‘. ## Markdown Grammar Markdown uses the same ‘0..999‘ relative coordinate grid as ‘ candidate_action ‘. Each UI element uses center - box coordinates : ‘[ content ]( type )< cx , cy , w , h >‘ Meaning : - ‘ cx , cy ‘ are the element center point . - ‘ w , h ‘ are the element width and height . - All four numbers are integers on the ‘0..999‘ grid . Its content is usually text , and it is generally larger than an icon . - ‘ input ‘: a visible editable field ; use its current value , otherwise its visible placeholder . - ‘ icon ‘: A small graphical symbol whose background color usually matches the webpage background . It may optionally have a black outline . - ‘ image ‘: A photograph or visual depicting natural scenes , people , or similar content , with boundaries clearly distinguishable from the webpage background . - ‘ toggle ‘: Any checkable element , such as a checkbox or radio button . - ‘ select ‘: A dropdown or expandable selection control . ### Toggle State - ‘[ ]‘ indicates unchecked , off , or unselected . - ‘[ x ]‘ indicates checked , on , or selected . - Clicking a toggle usually switches between ‘[ ]‘ and ‘[ x ]‘. - When a toggle state changes , keep the same label and coordinates . ### Select State - ‘[>]‘ indicates collapsed or closed . - ‘[ v ]‘ indicates expanded or open . - Clicking a closed select usually expands it and displays options nearby . - Clicking an open select closes it . ### Block Block description must be one of : - ‘ Navigation ‘ - ‘ Sidebar ‘ - ‘ Footer ‘ - ‘ Form ‘ - ‘ Table ‘ - ‘ Section ‘ ### Concrete Example [ Environment : Web ] - [ Block : Navigation ]<500,40,960,60> - [ Home ]( link )<80,40,80,30> - [ icon : menu ]( icon )<950,40,30,30> - [ Block : Sidebar ]<110,350,180,520> - [ ] [ Dark ]( toggle )<100,150,120,30> - [ x ] [ Sync ]( toggle )<100,200,120,30> - [>] [ More ]( select )<100,250,120,30> - [ Block : Form ]<590,210,720,200> - [ Query ]( input )<520,190,480,35> - [ Go ]( button )<850,190,100,35> - [ Block : Section ]<590,410,720,160> - [ v ] [ Mode ]( select )<340,370,160,30> - [ sample1 ]( text )<340,415,160,30> - [ sample2 ]( text )<340,460,160,30> - [ Block : Table ]<590,600,720,160> - [ Row ]( text )<360,580,200,25> - [ Block : Footer ]<500,960,960,60> - [ img : blue mountain lake at sunset ]( image )<160,960,240,30> ## Prediction Rules The top - to - bottom order of elements in the prediction should roughly match their order in the webpage viewport . Prioritize correct semantics and element types , then infer reasonable coordinate positions . For ‘ left_click ‘ / ‘ double_click ‘ / ‘ right_click ‘: - Locate the target element based on coordinates . - Predict visible navigation , pop - ups , menus , forms or selected states after the click . - right_click may open a context menu . For ‘ type_text ‘: - Write ‘ text ‘ into the currently focused or target input . For ‘ scroll ‘: - Predict visible content changes from signed relative - screen ‘ delta_x ‘ and ‘ delta_y ‘ integers in ‘[-999,999]‘; magnitude ‘999‘ is one full screen . Positive ‘ delta_y ‘ scrolls down , negative scrolls up ; positive ‘ delta_x ‘ scrolls right , negative scrolls left . For ‘ key_press ‘ / ‘ hotkey ‘: - ‘ ENTER ‘ is often used to submit forms , search , or confirm . - ‘ ESC ‘ is often used to close pop - ups , menus , or dropdowns . - ‘ CTRL / CMD + L ‘ often focuses the address bar ; ‘ CTRL / CMD + T ‘ often opens a new tab . For ‘ navigate ‘ / ‘ go_back ‘ / ‘ go_forward ‘ / ‘ refresh ‘: - Predict the visible page after browser navigation . For ‘ select_option ‘: - Update the visible value of the select , close the options list , and remove the old expanded options . For ‘ drag ‘: - Predict sorting , slider position or drag - and - drop result caused by dragging . For ‘ hover ‘ / ‘ move_to ‘: - A tooltip , hover menu , or highlighted state may appear . For ‘ wait ‘: - Predict natural changes such as loading completion , asynchronous results , or pop - ups appearing / disappearing . For ‘ clear ‘: - Clear the target input or the currently focused input area . For ‘ finish ‘ / ‘ fail ‘: - Finish and fail do not change the visible interface .

blocks.en: ⬇ # Independent Online - Mind2Web trajectory judgment You are an independent strict judge . Inspect this one trajectory only . The attached screenshots are ordered chronologically and correspond exactly to : ["0000. png ", "0001. png ", "..."] Use the screenshots and action log as evidence . The agent ’ s final answer and ‘ agent_finish ‘ status are untrusted claims , not proof of success . ## Success rule - Return success =1 only when the visual / action evidence proves every material requirement in the task instruction was completed . - For cart / form / state - changing tasks , require evidence of the resulting state ; reaching a relevant page or merely attempting the last action is insufficient . - For comparison or information tasks , require that the requested information was actually reached and visible / readable enough to answer the instruction . - If evidence is ambiguous , incomplete , contradicted , or ends at max steps , use 0. - Do not award success just because an action has action_status = SUCCESS ; that only means browser execution returned , not that the benchmark goal was achieved . ## Technical - failure rule - environment_technical_failure = true only for objective environment failures such as DNS / network / browser failure , persistent server error , inaccessible page , or an external blocking challenge that prevents evaluation . - model_technical_failure = true only for model / pipeline failures such as empty or malformed model output , generation / API failure , action parse failure , or an execution_error attributable to the agent pipeline . - Ordinary bad planning , wrong clicks , repetition , premature finish , and max_steps are task failures but are NOT model technical failures . - A successful task may still have a transient technical failure only if the trajectory clearly recovered and ultimately proves completion . ## Evidence payload { " task_id ": "< task_id >", " task_instruction ": "< task instruction >", " agent_final_answer ": "< agent final answer >", " reference_length ": "< reference length >", " run_metadata ": {}, " action_history ": [], " runtime_diagnostics ": { " raw_step_count ": 0, " execution_errors ": [] } } ## Output contract Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else : { " task_id ": "< task_id >", " success ": 0, " reason ": " one concise evidence - based sentence ", " key_evidence_steps ": [0], " key_evidence_screenshots ": ["0000. png "], " environment_technical_failure ": false , " model_technical_failure ": false , " technical_failure_type ": " none ", " technical_failure_reason ": "" } The success value must be integer 0 or 1. Evidence steps / screenshots must exist in the supplied trajectory . technical_failure_type must be one of none , environment , model , both and must agree with the two booleans .
blocks.zh: ⬇ 独立在线 - Mind2 网络轨迹判断 你是一个独立的严格法官。 检查这个轨迹 所附的截图按时间顺序排列,准确对应: ["00.00.png","0001.png",". 使用截图和动作日志作为证据 。 代理人的最终答案和`代理人_完成 ' 地位是不信任的主张,而不是成功的证据。 {\fn华文仿宋\fs16\1cHD1D1D1} 成功规则 - 返回成功 = 1 只有当视觉/ 动作证据证明任务指令中的所有实质性要求均已完成 。 - 对于手推车 / 形式 / 状态 - 变化的任务,需要生成状态的证据 ; 到达相关的一页或仅仅尝试最后的动作是不够的 。 - 对于比较或信息任务,要求所请求的信息实际到达并可见 / 可读到足以回答指令 。 如果证据模棱两可、不完整、相矛盾或以最大步骤结尾,则使用 0. - 不要仅仅因为一个动作具有 action_status = SUCCESS而授予成功;这只意味着浏览器执行返回,而不是基准目标已经实现. ^ 技术 - 故障规则 - 环境_ 技术_ 故障 = 仅针对 DNS / 网络/ 浏览器故障等客观环境故障, 持续的服务器错误, 无法访问的页面, 或外部阻塞挑战, 妨碍评价 。 - 型号_ technology_failure = 仅适用于型号/ 管线故障, 如空出或变形的型号输出, 生成/ API 失败, 动作剖析失败, 或可归于代理管线的执行- 错误规划, 点击错误, 重复, 过早完成, 最大_ 步骤都是任务失败, 但不是型号技术故障 。 - 成功的任务只有在轨迹清晰恢复并最终证明完成的情况下, 仍然可能有短暂的技术故障 。 {\fn华文仿宋\fs16\1cHD1D1D1} 证据有效载荷{"任务-id":" <任务-id","任务-指示":"任务指令","代理_最终_回答","参考-长":"参考长度","运行-元数据","动作-历史","运行时间-诊断","生_步_计数",":0","执行-罪犯",[}## 输出合同 返回一个 JSON 对象,没有其它: { "任务-id": " < 任务-id", "成功": 0, "理由": "一个简明的证据 - 基于句子", "关键_证据_步骤" : [0], "关键_证据_屏幕截图" : ["000. png"], "环境_技术_失败" : 虚假, "模型_技术_失败" : 虚假, "技术-失败-类型" : "无", "技术_失败-理性" : ""] 成功值必须是整数 0 或 1 。 证据步骤/截图必须存在于所提供的轨迹中。 技术_失败_类型必须是无之一, 环境,模型, 两者必须同意两个布尔。

blocks.en: ⬇ TASK CONTRACT Evaluate exactly one desktop Web UI screenshot sample . Return four independent quality scores from 0 to 100. Judge only the evidence in this call . Do not identify or guess the dataset , collection method , author , website , or benchmark . IMAGE ROLES Image A is the unannotated screenshot . Use Image A only for page_complexity . Image B is the same screenshot with thin black - and - white annotation outlines and small numeric box identifiers . SCORING RUBRIC 1. annotation_object_validity Definition : The proportion of evaluable annotations that correspond to a visually recognizable UI element or meaningful UI region . Atomic controls , text , images , groups , containers , navigation regions , content regions , and other structural blocks can be valid targets . Anchors : - 0: No usable annotation corresponds to a recognizable intended target , or annotation_state fixes this score at zero . - 25: Only a small minority of annotations have recognizable intended targets ; empty or background - only boxes dominate . - 50: Recognizable and unrecognizable intended targets are roughly balanced . - 75: Most annotations have recognizable intended targets , with a noticeable minority of empty , background - only , or unusable annotations . - 100: Essentially every evaluable annotation has a clearly recognizable intended target and source - level machine issues are absent or negligible . 2. boundary_alignment Definition : How well assessable original sides represent reasonable boundaries for recognizable target semantics . Atomic visual elements should have visually tight or appropriate interaction boundaries . Text or CSS - content labels may use content - oriented boxes . Structural regions may use semantic grouping boundaries . Anchors : - 0: Assessable sides are almost entirely unrelated to , or severely displaced from , their recognizable targets . - 25: Major displacement , excessive extent , or severe clipping affects most assessable original sides . - 50: Assessable original sides show a roughly even mix of reasonable and materially inaccurate placement . - 75: Most assessable original sides reasonably delimit their targets , with a noticeable minority that are loose , shifted , clipped , or undersized . - 100: Essentially all assessable sides closely match reasonable atomic , interaction , content , or structural boundaries for their targets . 3. label_semantic_reasonableness Definition : Whether each valid , recognizable target ’ s complete provided label set is semantically compatible with that target under the supplied ‘ classes ‘ table . Broad functional , visual , accessibility - role , atomic , and structural labels can all be reasonable . Compatible multi - label descriptions are valid . Anchors : - 0: Equal - weight semantic contributions are essentially all zero ; supplied labels are incompatible with their visible targets . - 25: Equal - weight semantic contributions average near one quarter ; most annotations have incompatible or largely incompatible label sets . - 50: Equal - weight semantic contributions average near one half , reflecting a roughly balanced mixture of compatible and incompatible labels within annotations . - 75: Equal - weight semantic contributions average near three quarters ; most annotations have fully or mostly compatible label sets , with a noticeable minority of mismatches . - 100: Equal - weight semantic contributions are essentially all one ; every supplied label is compatible with its visible target and supplied ontology . 4. page_complexity Definition : The amount , diversity , and depth of visible UI structure in Image A . Consider layout hierarchy , visible regions , component variety , information density , spatial relationships , typography , imagery , color relationships , and interaction affordances together . Anchors : - 0: Almost blank or visually empty , with essentially no discernible page structure or content . - 25: A sparse page with one simple region , few visible component types , and little hierarchy or information . - 50: A moderately structured page with several regions or component types and ordinary information density . - 75: Many visible regions and component types , with substantial hierarchy or dense spatial relationships . - 100: Exceptionally many diverse UI regions and components with very deep or dense visible relationships , regardless of presentation quality . OUTPUT CONTRACT Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else : { " sample_id ": "< sample_id >", " annotation_object_validity ": 0, " boundary_alignment ": 0, " label_semantic_reasonableness ": 0, " page_complexity ": 0 } Each score is an integer from 0 to 100. Copy sample_id from the supplied sample .
blocks.zh: TASK合同 精确评估一个桌面 Web UI 截图样本 。 返回4个独立质量分从0到100分. 只有这个电话中的证据 不识别或猜测数据集、收集方法、作者、网站或基准。 形象作用 图像 A 是未附加说明的截图 。 只使用图像 A 表示页面_ 复杂度 。 图片 B 是相同的截图, 带有细黑- 和- 白色注解轮廓和小数字框标识符 。 1. 注解_对象-有效性定义:可评价注解中与可视识别的UI元素或有意义的UI区域对应的比例。 原子控制、文本、图像、组、容器、导航区域、内容区域和其他结构块可以成为有效目标。 锚: - 0:没有可用注释对应可识别的预期目标,或注释_状态将这个分数固定为零. - 25:只有一小部分说明有可识别的预期目标;空的或背景的----只有方框占主导地位。 - 50:可识别和不可识别的预期目标大致平衡。 - 75:大多数说明有可识别的预期目标,其中明显少数是空的、背景的 -- -- 或无法使用的说明。 2. 边界_对接 定义:可评估的原始面如何代表可识别的目标语义的合理边界。 原子视觉元素应有视觉上紧凑或适当的相互作用界限。 文本或 CSS - 内容标签可使用内容 - 面向框 。 结构区域可能使用语义分组边界。 锚: - 0:可评估方几乎完全与其可识别目标无关,或严重流离失所。 - 25:主要流离失所、范围过大或严重剪接影响到大多数可评估的原始方面。 - 50:可评估的原始侧面大致均匀地组合了合理和物质不准确的放置。 - 75:大多数可评估的原始方合理划定其目标,其中明显的少数部分松散、转移、剪接或尺寸过小。 3. 标签_语义_合理性 定义:每个有效、可识别的目标的完整提供的标签集是否与所提供的 " 类 " 表下的目标完全相容。 广义的功能性,可视性,可取性 - 角色,原子和结构标签都可以合理. 兼容多标签描述有效 。 指针: -0:等重语义贡献基本上都是零;提供的标签与其可见的目标不相容. - 25:平均近四分之一的等重语义贡献;大多数说明有不兼容或基本不相容的标签集。 - 50:平均近一半的等重语义贡献,反映了说明中兼容和不相容标签的大致平衡混合。 - 75:平均约四分之三的等重语义贡献;大多数说明有完全或大部分相容的标签集,明显少有不匹配。 - 100: 等重语义贡献基本上是全部的;每个提供的标签都与其可见的目标和提供的本体学相符。 4. 页面复杂度 定义:图像A中可见的UI结构的量,多样性和深度. 考虑布局等级、可见区域、组件种类、信息密度、空间关系、打字、图像、颜色关系,以及相互作用。 锁定: - 0: 几乎为空白或视空,基本上没有明显的页面结构或内容。 - 25:缺少一个简单区域的页面,可见组件类型很少,结构或信息也很少。 - 50:具有若干区域或组成部分类型和普通信息密度的中度结构页面。 - 75:许多可见区域和成份类型,具有实质性的等级或密集的空间关系。 外包合同 完全返回一个 JSON 对象而无其它 : { " sample_id " : " sample_id " , " anotation_object_valuity " : 0, " 边界-对齐 " : 0, " 标签-语义_合理性 " : 0, " page_complexity " : 0 } 每分从0到100的整数. 从提供的样本复制样本_ID。
